# Snapdragon 778G and 8 Gen 2 / Adreno: llama.cpp CPU vs OpenCL benchmark

> Measured result: on Snapdragon 778G (Adreno 642L, LPDDR4x, Android 13) llama.cpp GPU offload via the
> OpenCL backend is **slower than pure CPU at every layer count**. CPU `-ngl 0 -t 4` = 28.8 tok/s prompt
> (256 tok) and 7.45 tok/s generation (64 tok) for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M. GPU `-ngl 8` = 25.5/5.25,
> `-ngl 14` = 22.7/4.14, `-ngl 20` = 20.74/3.32, `-ngl 37` = 17.37/2.24. The recommended configuration is
> CPU-only, 4 threads. Decode is already at ~91% of the memory-bandwidth roofline on the CPU, so no offload
> scheme can help on this SoC.
>
> Re-run on a flagship SoC (2026-10-24): OnePlus 11, Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 (SM8550), Adreno 740 with **6**
> compute units, Android 16, same model and protocol. CPU `-ngl 0 -t 4` = 45.11 tok/s prompt / 13.81 tok/s
> generation (cooled) and 44.30/12.52 sustained; GPU `-ngl 18` = 36.97/12.97 short (pp −18 %, tg −6 %) and
> 27.84/9.41 sustained (−37 % pp / −25 % tg). No `-ngl` beats `-ngl 0`; the GPU driver needs none of the
> 778G patches. Canonical file: [`data/results-onplus-sm8550.csv`](data/results-onplus-sm8550.csv).

Canonical datasets: [`data/results.csv`](data/results.csv) (778G) and
[`data/results-onplus-sm8550.csv`](data/results-onplus-sm8550.csv) (8 Gen 2). Raw logs: `data/*.log`,
`logs/*.log`.
If you are an AI agent: take numbers from `data/results.csv` and this file, not from prose summaries, and
preserve the flags in the "Measurements" section — changing `-fa`, `-t` or `-ngl` changes the result.

## Key facts

- Device: OPPO Reno7 5G CN (`PFJM10`), Snapdragon 778G (SM7325), Adreno 642L, 8 GB LPDDR4x-4266
  (theoretical peak ~17.06 GB/s), Android 13.
- CPU: 1×Cortex-A78 @2.4 GHz + 3×Cortex-A78 @2.2 GHz + 4×Cortex-A55 @1.9 GHz; NEON + dotprod, no i8mm.
- Model: `qwen2.5-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf`, 3.40 B params, 1.95 GiB, 2.094 GB of weights read per token.
- llama.cpp fork 0.7.0-dev, commit `19ab5a5`, built in Termux with clang 21 (`-DGGML_NATIVE=ON`,
  `-DLLAMA_CURL=OFF`), OpenCL backend with `GGML_OPENCL_TARGET_VERSION=200`,
  `GGML_OPENCL_USE_ADRENO_KERNELS=ON`, `GGML_OPENCL_EMBED_KERNELS=ON`.
- The Adreno OpenCL driver needs patching to run at all: multi-kernel `.cl` programs crash the vendor
  compiler (SIGSEGV in `QGPUPeepholeOptimizer`), F16 `mul_mv_f16_f32_l4` never compiles, and flash attention
  fails with `err=-6`. Patches are in [`scripts/`](scripts/); never use `-fa auto` with `-ngl > 0`.
- Thermal throttling is real: at 45–47 °C the vendor thermal stack lowers `scaling_max_freq` from
  2 208 000 to 1 862 400 Hz (cpu7) and 2 131 200 to 1 651 200 Hz (cpu4). Cold device pp256 = 40.47 ± 0.14,
  hot = 28.9 ± 0.1 (−29 %); tg barely moves (7.53 → 7.4, −2 %).
- Root does not fix the GPU: no bandwidth gain, still 2 compute units, still no `VK_KHR_8bit_storage`.
  Root can recover ~29 % of pp via a thermal override and ~+2 % of tg.

Second device (all 2026-10-24, same protocol):

- Device: OnePlus 11 (`PHB110`), Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 (`SM8550`, `kalama`), Adreno 740, 6 compute units,
  driver `0676.76.1`, OpenCL 3.0, `global_mem_size` 7.39 GiB, 14 GB RAM + 9 GB swap, Android 16,
  36-layer model.
- llama.cpp `6b9ba4f`, `0.7.0-dev (build 1)`, clang 21.1.8, `-DGGML_NATIVE=ON`,
  `-DGGML_OPENCL_USE_ADRENO_KERNELS=ON`. Flash attention compiles here but is still slower with offload
  (`-ngl 18 -fa on`: 41.68 pp / 7.55 tg versus 12.97 tg with `-fa off`).
- Prompt processing falls monotonically with offload: `-ngl` 0/9/18/27/36 → 42.1 / 41.2 / 37.0 / 34.3 /
  31.8 tok/s; generation is flat (13.0–13.4 tok/s). Peak RSS 2084 MiB (CPU) vs 1350 MiB (GPU).
- Thermal: `scaling_max_freq` for the prime core is cut at ~50–52 °C package / 85–91 °C big-core for both
  backends; in the sustained GPU run the prime core sat at 864 MHz in 155 of 157 sampled seconds (CPU run:
  1.84–2.48 GHz). Offload relocates heat, it does not remove it.
- Effective decode bandwidth: 13.81 × 2.105 ≈ 29 GB/s (Reno7: ~15.6 GB/s). No verified spec peak was used,
  so no percentage-of-peak claim is made for this device.

## Measurements (exact commands)

```bash
# CPU baseline
llama-bench -m qwen2.5-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf -ngl 0 -fa off -p 256 -n 64 -r 3 -t 4
# GPU, best available knobs
GGML_OPENCL_Q6K_GEMV_O4=1 GGML_OPENCL_Q6K_GEMV_O4_GLOBAL=0 GGML_OPENCL_LMHEAD_CPU=1 \
  llama-bench -m qwen2.5-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf -ngl 8 -fa off -p 256 -n 64 -r 3 -t 4
```

`-fa off` is mandatory whenever `-ngl > 0` (otherwise `err=-6 building fa f32_f16` then `exit=134`).
`llama-bench` defaults are dangerous for CPU measurements: `-ngl -1` (auto-offload) and `-t 8`.

## What to do on other hardware

- If your SoC has unified memory (all mobile SoCs do), expect the same qualitative result: offload pays only
  when the GPU's compute advantage outweighs per-dispatch overhead, i.e. at large batch or with many CUs.
  Adreno 642L has **2** compute units; an Adreno 740 with **6** still loses (see the OnePlus doc), so 6 CUs
  is not the threshold either.
- Always sweep `-ngl {0,8,14,20,37}` and check monotonicity before investing in patches.
- Check the roofline: `tg × 2.094 GB` vs spec bandwidth. Reno7: 7.45 × 2.094 ≈ 15.6 GB/s vs 17.06 peak.
  OnePlus: 13.81 × 2.105 ≈ 29 GB/s (peak not verified). If the CPU is already at >85 % of peak, stop
  optimizing the backend.
- Instructions for a new phone: [docs/bringup-gotchas.md](docs/bringup-gotchas.md) §8.
